text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Aviation minister says any airline that hikes domestic air fares by 200 percent from Monday as the airline operators association has resolved to do will be grounded.
- Secretariat of Micro-Credit Summit in Washington D.C. appoints Nigeria's first lady Maryam Abacha as one of its advocates because of her Family Support Programme.
- Five days into registration of voters for future elections, complaints grow; electoral commission says no evidence to back the complaints
- U.S. State Department in a statement released in the Nigerian capital Abuja deplores latest bomb blast in Lagos on Wednesday in which eight people were wounded.
- Fuel scarcity hits southwestern city of Ibadan with long queues at pump stations on Friday.

- Three Nigerian professors to join two others from Ghana in the United States to study the possibility of genetic link between African-American diabetics and their African forebears, says U.S. information service.

- As interest rates slide nationwide, Petroleum Trust Fund, which disburses money accruing from a 1994 hike in pump prices, slashes by half to between 4-5 percent the rate it now demands from banks for depositing funds with them.
- United Nigeria Congress Party, deemed to be the biggest of the five registered to compete for political power, raises 150 million naira to campaign in next month's municipal poll.
